target.title: refactor(qa): retire the standalone Matrix QA runtime
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Matrix QA had two independently maintained execution systems: the canonical QA Lab scenario host with transport adapters, and a standalone `qa-matrix` plugin with its own CLI runtime, scenario catalog, profiles, artifacts, retries, and release orchestration. The duplicate path drifted from QA Lab and made release status, evidence, credentials, and lifecycle behavior depend on which Matrix runner was selected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Make QA Lab the single owner of Matrix QA. The maintained Matrix transport lifecycle now lives behind QA Lab's registered `live:matrix` adapter, and `pnpm openclaw qa matrix` remains only as a thin QA Lab selector that maps `all|fast|release|transport` (or explicit scenario ids) into the canonical `runQaSuiteCommand()` host.

This removes the `extensions/qa-matrix` package/plugin, private runner/catalog, Matrix-only artifact format, sharded workflow jobs, package registrations, generated catalog entries, and obsolete docs. Release checks and manual QA Live runs use one reusable workflow job, one status output, and the standard QA Lab evidence contract.

Compatibility fallback is intentionally not retained: the removed package and private runtime were unshipped maintainer internals, and preserving them would recreate the forbidden second execution path. The dependency is PR #101055 exact head `395b864d2037ab9a3d50416fca2eb4ecdc49efa4`, whose `createQaChannelDriverLifecycle()` seam owns Matrix lifecycle through the QA transport registry.

## User Impact

Maintainers and release managers now get one Matrix QA implementation and one evidence format. Focused release proof still uses `pnpm openclaw qa matrix --profile release`; comprehensive maintained Matrix proof uses `--profile all`. Both commands execute the same QA Lab scenario host through the same Matrix adapter and write `qa-suite-report.md`, `qa-suite-summary.json`, and `qa-evidence.json`.

There is no user-facing runtime change to the shipped Matrix channel plugin. Packaged OpenClaw releases continue to omit the private QA Lab tooling.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kwx5tzg8m7m0n9h993t4ww8e` (`violet-shrimp`), exact candidate tree:
  - Full `pnpm build` — passed.
  - QA Lab Matrix CLI/adapter/substrate, lifecycle, workflow, SDK, plugin registry, and package inventory tests — passed.
  - `OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 ... matrix-channel-driver.lifecycle.live.test.ts` — 2/2 passed; both `live:matrix` and `crabline:matrix` exercised all five lifecycle scenarios.
  - `pnpm openclaw qa matrix --profile release --provider-mode mock-openai ...` — 2/2 scenarios passed; standard QA Lab artifacts verified.
  - `pnpm openclaw qa matrix --profile all --provider-mode mock-openai ...` — 5/5 scenarios passed: channel baseline, allowlist hot reload, restart resume, replay dedupe, and post-restart room continuation; standard QA Lab artifacts verified.
  - `pnpm plugins:inventory:check`, `pnpm docs:map:check`, and `pnpm format:docs:check` — passed.
  - `pnpm check:changed --staged` — passed, including full tsgo typecheck, oxlint shards, database-first guard, package/shrinkwrap guards, and import-cycle check.
- Baseline note: the existing Crabline smoke-profile test in `extensions/qa-lab/src/cli.runtime.test.ts` fails identically on clean dependency head `395b864d2037ab9a3d50416fca2eb4ecdc49efa4` because its current taxonomy selection spans multiple channel ids; this PR does not modify that path.
- Fresh Codex autoreview on the final staged bundle — clean after one accepted workflow-expression fix, no accepted/actionable findings (confidence 0.86).
- Workflow contract test `test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts` — 42/42 passed after explicit reusable lane selection.
- Exact-head focused release proof: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28839918390 — passed; exact SHA validated, secretless mock Matrix release profile passed, and all non-Matrix lanes were skipped.
- Exact-head full QA Live proof: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28839920118 — Matrix passed; full workflow failed only in the independent existing Telegram `telegram-repeated-command-authorization` scenario after both retries, while dedicated Telegram live scenarios passed 5/5.
- Exact PR head: `17549c0727e52150d66b51ea9dae5c3aefac0cc5`.
